rows.47:7138:
"The flower bed's still there, isn't it?
Every year the hydrangeas bloom so beautifully.
Bright red hydrangeas...
Did you know?
Those flowers bloom red by sucking up human blood."
Heh, that's such a common story.
Huh? Wait, wasn't it cherry trees that have corpses buried under them?
"You don't seem to take me seriously, but a lot of people really have died there.
Even members of the gardening club have died, you know."{p}
rows.47:72bc:
Even when he tells me that, it just doesn't click for me.
That flower bed isn't very big, and it's well tended but totally ordinary. It doesn't seem like a place with that kind of dark history at all.
"Hmm, I can tell from your face you don't believe me.
Forget it.
I was going to ask you to do a certain interview, but at this rate, there's no way it'd make a good article."
Whaaat★
If that's the case, you should've said so first!
Then I would've answered more seriously...
Is it too late now?
But just as I thought that, {a} was already packing up to go home.
"Sorry for making you come all this way today.
Well, good work."{p}
rows.47:7660:
Yep, I was right.
The hydrangea season's almost over, but the red flowers are in full bloom.
The color of hydrangea flowers changes with the soil they grow in, you know.
Blue if it's alkaline, and if it's acidic... red.
Saying they suck up human blood... As a story, that's way too common. Nobody could expect me to believe it.
Oh?
There's something under the flowers.
It looks like a red umbrella.
Did someone forget it? It still looks brand new.
I'll just touch it a little.
I pick up the umbrella ever so gently...
What a vivid red.
Oh, there's a name written on the handle.
Um... Yukari Tachibana...?
Is that how you read it?
I've never heard the name. Is she in the gardening club?{p}
rows.47:78c8:
Wh-what?
Did I just hear a voice...?{p}
rows.47:7918:
S-see, I knew it!
But why... it's starting to sound more and more like my own voice.{p}
rows.47:79a4:
I'm getting really irritated.
I won't stand for it anymore!
That person doesn't understand how I feel at all!
I hate them!
I hate them so much!{p}
rows.47:7a24:
(I want to kill them!)
Yes, I hate them so much I want to kill them!{p}
rows.47:7a78:
Just then!
"Oh, Taguchi, so you were here after all.
After that story, right?
I figured you'd come here."
It was {a}.
"The thing is... um... hmm, how do I put this..."
What is he trying to say?
He's fidgeting and can't keep still.{p}
rows.47:7be0:
"I'll kill you☆"
I...
I brought the umbrella down at {a}'s throat.
Again and again...
When I came to, I was in a sea of blood.
He was lying there beside me...
(Heh heh. Now then, it's your turn to die.){p}
rows.47:7cb8:
That's not my voice!
But it was different from the voice I heard before, too.
Whose voice was that?
Why should I have to die?
Oh, but my hands are gripping the umbrella on their own.
They press its tip right up against my throat...
It's not me doing this.
I don't want to die!
But... I killed {a}, didn't I?
Maybe I have to die after all.
Why did I kill him?
What was he trying to tell me back then?
All sorts of things are spinning around in my head.
So it's true that right before you die, your whole life flashes before your eyes like a revolving lantern.{p}
rows.47:7ea8:
It hurts☆
My throat burns with pain!
The sound of bones shattering echoes deep inside my ears.
It seems the tip of the umbrella went right through my neck.
Lukewarm liquid is gushing down my back.
So you can still be conscious even like this.
But somehow I feel sleepy.
I'm going to fall asleep like this forever.
And the last voice I heard was...{p}
rows.47:7fd4:
(Hee hee hee... I'm so happy. Now beautiful flowers will bloom again. Lots and lots of beautiful, beautiful red flowers will bloom. Just like when I died...)
So it was the ghost of someone from the gardening club.{p}
rows.47:8088:
"Oh, yes.
I know about it."
A teacher told me about it before.
When they tore down the old school building, human skeletons turned up and it caused a huge uproar.
But I don't know the details very well.
"Um, you mean the skeletons turning up?"
"Right.
That story's famous, isn't it?
People said all sorts of things, like there was an air-raid shelter under the old school building, or that there were lots of bodies of war dead around there."
He seems kind of excited.
He's talking with sweat on his nose.{p}
rows.47:8244:
When they tore down the old school building, a lot of accidents happened.
People said it was the curse of the skeletons, and some pretty large-scale purification rites were held.
Back then, I'd been assigned to write an article about the school's seven wonders.
At the time, I had my own senior, a guy named Hino, gather people who knew a lot about the school's seven wonders.{p}
rows.47:8374:
I see.
I knew you'd say that.
Then I'll gather seven people who know a lot about the school's seven wonders.
...Let's see, the day after tomorrow would be good.
Could you come to the club room again the day after tomorrow?
I'll have everything settled with the seven of them by then.{p}
rows.47:8518:
Geez, he only acts like my senior at times like this...
But I absolutely don't want to!
I'm no good with scary stuff.
"I don't want to."
"Don't say that.
This is all for your own good.
Oh, I know, have this.
Don't be shy, drink up."{p}
rows.47:85e0:
With that, he brought out some juice for me.
"Is it really okay to use the newspaper club's equipment for something like that?"
He'd been hiding juice in the newspaper club's fridge for storing film.
"Aw, don't be so uptight. Look, it's nice and cold.
Which one do you want?"
The juice wasn't in cans, but in mini plastic bottles.{p}
rows.47:8730:
Well, I am thirsty...
Maybe I'll have one?
Oh, it's tea.
But it's awfully grassy-smelling tea.
Is this that Sanbura tea he told me about before?
"Huh, you know that tea, Taguchi?
It's a sister product of a tea called Sanbura tea. It just came out."
It's true, the label says Yonbura tea.
What a lazy name.
I take a sip...{p}
rows.47:88a4:
Oh, it's actually pretty good.
The smell's a little hard to take, but the taste isn't bad.
"How is it?
Good?"
"Yes. I don't know how to describe it, but it tastes pretty good."
"I see, glad to hear it.
When I drank it, it was so foul it couldn't have been of this world."
Are his taste buds and mine really that different?
Come to think of it, he's happily drinking orange juice.
It's way too sweet for me, but he seems to think it tastes good.
Somehow, that makes sense to me.
I gulped down the rest of the tea in one go.{p}
rows.47:8ab0:
Hmm, how should I put it?
This refreshing feeling.
My head feels clear, like my memory's gotten better.
If I concentrate, I can remember all sorts of things.
From what happened just now all the way back to before I started kindergarten...
If I really tried, I could probably remember being in my mother's womb.{p}
rows.47:8bbc:
Huh, what was that scene just now?
A girl is lying there, bleeding.
It looks like she was in an accident, but did something like that ever happen?
Wait a minute, the face of the girl lying there...★
No way, what kind of joke is this!
It's my face☆
"That's right, that girl is you.
Mayumi Taguchi."{p}
rows.47:8cd4:
"{a}...?"
Can he see my memories?
If that's me lying there, I must have been hurt.
But I don't have a single injury anywhere...
"You died in an accident on the day of the entrance ceremony.
It was just so sudden that you didn't notice you'd died.
And you had lingering attachments too, so you've ended up wandering like this.
That drink just now, you see, tastes awful to the living.
Because it's a drink for the dead."{p}
rows.47:8e6c:
Oh, I see...
Listening to his voice, I remembered everything.
That day, on my way to the entrance ceremony, I was in an accident on the street in front of this school.
A car came plowing into me at a terrifying speed.
I must have died instantly.
But to think I kept going to school without even noticing I was dead...
"Now, you understand, don't you?
If you wander too long, you'll be absorbed by the evil spirits that infest this school.
You'd better pass on soon.
Now, these six will guide you to the spirit world."{p}
rows.47:9034:
Before I knew it, six men and women in white robes were standing beside me.
They were all smiling warmly, wrapped in white light.
"Thank you, {a}.
But who are you, really...?"
"I'm just an ordinary person.
It's only that I went through something out of the ordinary once, and ended up knowing far too much about this world."
But he seems to be shining the brightest of all...
And then I was wrapped in white light too...
Even far away, I could still see his light, tiny.
When that light disappears, the person called Mayumi Taguchi will be completely dead.
If I can be reborn, I want to meet him again...{p}
rows.47:9260:
Actually, I think I won't go after all.
I'm just not in the mood.
The sky looks strange too. On a day like this, it's best to hurry home and relax.
I slipped out of the classroom so my senior wouldn't spot me.
"Oh, Taguchi, off to the seven wonders meeting now?"
The moment I stepped into the hallway, someone called out to me.{p}
rows.47:93f8:
What? There's nobody here.
Was I hearing things?
I keep thinking 'don't get caught, don't get caught,' so I'm hearing things that aren't there.
Come on, if I just hurry home and get a nice, looong rest, I'll be fine.
Thinking that, I started walking...{p}
rows.47:94d8:
"Being in the newspaper club sure is tough.
You've got the seven wonders meeting now, right?"
The one who'd called out to me was a fat guy.
"Um..."{p}"Well, good luck."{p}
rows.47:9560:
Saying only that, he walked briskly away.
Oh, he just went into the restroom.
But have I met him somewhere before?
I don't remember.
Oh well.
I've got to get home before my senior finds me.{p}
rows.47:9700:
"The seven wonders, I hear.
Heh heh heh, liars get killed, you know.
Be careful you don't get killed."
This woman's a little scary.
I wish she wouldn't say things like getting killed.
Or is she trying to say I'm a liar?{p}
rows.47:97cc:
She flashed an eerie smile and walked off down the hall without a sound.
I've got a really bad feeling about this...{p}What should I do? Should I go to the newspaper club after all?
rows.47:98a0:
I'm completely worn out just getting this far.
I really want to go home now.{p}
rows.47:9908:
"Well, well, you look tired, young lady."
Sigh, here comes somebody else.
It was a man with a smirk on his face.
"I may not look it, but I'm a spirit medium.
Shall I read your future for you?
Mm-hm, you're on your way to the seven wonders meeting.
Oh, you don't have to answer.
I already know everything."
What kind of day is this?!
One weirdo after another!{p}
rows.47:9a4c:
Without answering him at all, I changed my shoes and left the school building.
He seemed to be yelling something behind me, but I'm not going to care. Not going to care.{p}
rows.47:9adc:
There were a few people dotted around the sports field.
It's a long way to the school gate, too.
I hurried toward the gate.
What's going on?
The people scattered around the field seem to be slowly closing in on me...
"Do you think you'd die instantly if you jumped off the roof?"
"Have you seen my Rubelize?"
"Here, missy, have some candy."
"I'm looking for someone to play poker with..."{p}
rows.47:9c48:
W-wait... wait a minute!
What is with these people★
There are even people here who aren't students!
I want to go home!
Please! Everybody, get out of the way☆{p}
rows.47:9ce4:
...In the end, my wish was in vain, and I wound up in front of the newspaper club room.
Are all the members here already?{p}
rows.47:9d68: Timidly, I opened the club room door, and★{p}
rows.47:9dac:
The one there was a girl who looked exactly like me.
The color of her indoor shoes was for third-years, so she's my senior.
Yes, she's a lovely person with a calm, mature air.
She's staring hard at my face.
Is she surprised because we look so alike?
Or so I thought, when
"No waaay, to think I'd run into you in a place like this!"
she said, and burst out laughing.
My image of her as 'calm and mature' crumbled a little.
But she pulled me into her arms and kept laughing, patting me on the back.
What on earth is going on?
"Ahaha, sorry for laughing all of a sudden.
I never dreamed I'd run into you in a place like this."
Phew, she finally let me go.
"Um, who are you...?"
"Hee hee, the time will come when you'll find out.
Let's see, all I can tell you right now is... this school's a weird place, but hang in there. That's about it."
"Um..."
"Now, go on home.
It's dangerous to stay here too late."{p}
rows.47:a0f4:
And so I left the club room as if I'd been thrown out.
What was that?
Honestly...!
I tried to open the club room door one more time.{p}
rows.47:a184:
Huh? It's locked.
Whaaat?
"Hey, Taguchi, you're early."
What? {a}?
"Nobody's here yet, right?"{p}
rows.47:a200: With that, he unlocked the door and went into the club room.{p}
rows.47:a2dc:
Then, after {a} left, six men and women gathered.
Just one more member to go...{p}
rows.47:a344:
I think he's an unpleasant person.
I mean, he's always kind of playing dumb.
He says his life changed after he met someone called Kazama.
He's just trying to blame someone else for how weird he is.{p}
rows.47:a40c:
But what could this talk be about?
A really important talk...
Don't tell me he wants to make me club president someday.
Oh, that would be such a problem.
I'd have no idea what kind of articles to make from then on.{p}
rows.47:a4e4:
Maybe I'll do an article on that dreamy senior from the basketball team.
I'll say 'I'm here for an interview!' and we'll have a nice friendly chat.
Ooh, what a dilemma.
But... I can't help hoping a little.
Hee hee.{p}
rows.47:a5a0:
Really, what should I do?
Should I go hear what {a} has to say?
rows.47:a5e0: Go hear what he has to say
rows.47:a5fc:
If he says it's important, then I've definitely got to hear it.
Okay, off to the club room.
Hee hee...
I hope it's good news.{p}

notes: 47:70c8: the scolding line is read as {a}'s reaction to the 'flower bed' answer; 7138 continues his speech.
47:7660: hydrangea soil colours kept as the source states (alkaline blue, acidic red), though reality is the reverse.
47:9adc/9908/94d8/9700: cameo lines (Arai roof, Iwashita's Rubelize, Candy Granny, poker; fat man = Hosoda, medium = Kazama, woman = Iwashita) left unnamed as in the source.
